text.p: Bindley Western Industries Inc said Friday it continues to explore alternatives that would allow it to spin off the majority of its Priority Healthcare business to its shareholders on a tax-free basis.
This would be consistent with a ruling received from the Internal Revenue Services in June, 1996.

"Our objective is to accomplish this by the end of 1997," Chairman William Bindley said. "As a rapidly growing specialty distributor and disease management company, opportunities for Priority Healthcare appear even more attractive than in the past, especially as a stand alone company."
In 1996, Priority Healthcare increased sales by 30 percent to $160 million and almost doubled its operating earnings.

Earlier, Bindley Western reported record earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.43 a share, up from $0.38 a year ago. Sales increased 20 percent to $1.57 billion in the fourth quarter from $1.31 billion.
For the year, sales increased 14 percent to $5.32 billion from $4.67 billion. Earnings, before charges, rose to $1.56 a share from $1.42.
Bindley Western is a large drug wholesaler.
